regenerable_on: any guest running bazarr with its API reachable and its key in hand, staged as harness/bin/se-capture-guest's bazarr case expects: SE_BAZARR_URL and SE_BAZARR_API_KEY in the capturing environment, forwarded to the guest as the header the app accepts. A freshly started bazarr with no languages profile reproduces the health issue below without any arranging — it is what the app says about itself before anybody configures it — but the version string moves with the image, so a re-stage re-reads the anchors by hand in the same change or they are asserting an instance that is gone.
anonymisation_note: Through the gate, and no substitution was needed — the run reported zero. The status document is the app reporting on itself (its own release, the image's package string, the Python and SQLite versions, the platform tuple, its core count) and the health document is one stock sentence bazarr writes for every install with no languages profile. The field says the gate RAN, not that values were rewritten; harness/scrub/bazarr.json states the two bounds under which that classification holds — the install paths are the container image's and not an operator's, and the timezone is the container default — and the independent detectors were run over the committed bytes afterwards.
note:
One instance, two documents, ONE row. `/api/system/status` and `/api/system/health` are separate requests answered by separate documents, and they feed a single object — so a port that published a row per document, or that keyed the collection on the path, gets a different commit count from the same payloads.

What this variant exists to teach is that a bazarr row is mostly about what it does NOT say. Four of the six facts this collection can carry are absent here, and each is absent for a different reason, which is why the anchors assert four absences beside two values. SonarrVersion and RadarrVersion are absent because bazarr answers them as EMPTY STRINGS — the members are present in the document and hold `""` — so the reference's `if data.get(member)` drops them, and a port that published a fact whenever the key existed emits two facts of empty string and fails. ConfigMissing is absent because both receipts were supplied; StatusUnobservable is absent because the API answered.

The health list is mirrored whole and ungraded, because bazarr does not grade it: the app hands back a flat array of {object, issue} pairs and the collection folds each to one sentence, `object: issue`. One issue here, so HealthIssues carries one string — a port that published the pair as a dict, or that kept only one half, fails the value anchor.

Stated bounds, because a specimen shows one instance on one day.

This bazarr is wired to NEITHER manager, so `sonarr_version` and `radarr_version` are empty and the two facts they would produce are exercised by no committed pair. A port blind to both reproduces this capture exactly and is wrong about every bazarr doing the job bazarr exists for. That blindness is owned by the differential guard, under the `bazarr-wired-managers` operator, with a9_manager_version_blind.py as its subject.

The entry folded here carries BOTH members. The reference falls back to whichever half it has when one is missing (`issue or subject`), and no bazarr this capture has seen produces a half-populated entry, so that arm is reached by nothing here.

The API answered, so this variant exercises no failure path at all. A missing SE_BAZARR_URL (absent, and the one decline that retires), an incomplete receipt (a row carrying ConfigMissing), and a configured instance whose API is dark (a row carrying StatusUnobservable) are three different statements this collector must make and no committed capture stages any of them.

And the row carries values only: no names family, no absent list, no unobservable record, no relation assertion. bazarr publishes no identifier that survives a rename — the object's native name is the constant `bazarr` — so law 1 has nothing here to carry, and the three non-value channels are unvisited.

anchors_note:
Read off payloads/api-system-status.json and payloads/api-system-health.json by hand at staging, before any stream existed, which is what makes them an authority the reference-generated half is not. Each was then corrupted in a scratch copy and the pair re-judged, so every one below has been SEEN to fail.

The object is named `bazarr` because that is the row's native name — the id the adapter mints is `instance:bazarr` and the collator derives it from the declared `instance` prefix and this name, so an anchor on the id would be asserting the collator's work rather than the collector's.

Version 1.6.0 is `data.bazarr_version`, and deliberately not `data.package_version`, which sits beside it holding `v1.6.0-ls360 by linuxserver.io`. The two are the same release spelled two ways and only one of them is a version; a port that read the packager's string publishes something no comparison across hosts can use, and fails here.

HealthIssues is anchored as the WHOLE list, one string long, because the fold is the derivation: `object` and `issue` joined by `: `. Three wrong ports fail on it and each fails differently — one that published the raw {object, issue} dict, one that published only the issue sentence, and one that joined with a different separator. The list form also pins that this is a list of one and not a bare string.

The four absences are the half a value anchor cannot state, and each names a different reason a fact does not apply.

SonarrVersion and RadarrVersion are absent because bazarr answers `""` for both — the members are PRESENT in the document, holding the empty string — so the anchors discriminate between omission and the wrong spelling a port reaches for, which is publishing a fact whose value is `""`. This is the same shape docker's five absences catch, where Labels is a dict without the key and Ports is a literal [].

ConfigMissing is absent because SE_BAZARR_URL and SE_BAZARR_API_KEY were both supplied at capture. Under replay the receipts are pinned in the seam rather than read from the replaying machine's environment, and this anchor is what makes that pin load-bearing: unpinned, the adapter finds no key on whatever workstation is replaying and publishes `ConfigMissing: ["SE_BAZARR_API_KEY"]` — a statement about the wrong machine, from a variant whose payloads are the API answering. Removing the pin turns this anchor red, which is where that was checked.

StatusUnobservable is absent because the API answered. It is the one fact whose presence would mean the collection is reporting a failure rather than a reading, so it is anchored absent for the same reason the commit count is anchored: a port that fell into its error arm on every run would still emit a row and still commit one object.

commit_objects 1 is the count of instances these two documents describe, and it is anchored because absence is not the only way to lose a collection: a port that emitted one row per document satisfies every fact anchor above and reports 2 here.

Deliberately not anchored: `start_time`, `cpu_cores`, `operating_system`, `python_version`, `database_engine`, `database_migration`, `bazarr_directory`, `bazarr_config_directory` and `timezone`. Every one of them is in the payload and none reaches the row — a fact must be cited by an opinion, used in identity or a relation, or be part of the declared answer (DESIGN 15) — so anchoring one would assert something this collection does not publish. `start_time` in particular is a wall-clock reading that a re-stage cannot reproduce, which is the same reason unbound's pair leaves `time.now` alone.
